pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: Migration 0002 adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all three existing rows are 0 and that the CHECK rejects 2.
'AC-2' test asserts '★ Second item' with the others unmarked; item() in src/index.js renders the star.
'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and expects id order [First, Third]; the query uses ORDER BY id.
'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all give the full list in id order.

The late commit 5b3b37b renamed the test so it no longer names AC-5 (now 'each view links to the other'). It also rewrote the AC text to 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a followable step. The spec records no owner decision or date for the edit. So no test names AC-5 and the review step demonstrates nothing. The code does render both links.
'AC-6' requests Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__ and expects 400 with no <li>. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn.

findings.what: Commit 5b3b37b, 'Follow-up edits', altered acceptance item AC-5 after the go. It appended '— verified by review: checked by hand' in the middle of the sentence, which garbles the text. 'Checked by hand' is not a followable step. The spec has no decision recording an owner call and date for the change.
findings.fix: Revert the spec edit. Keep AC-5 as originally written, covered by a test that names AC-5. If the owner really wants a review-only item, record their decision with a date and give a concrete step.

findings.what: The same commit removed the 'AC-5:' prefix from the link test's title. The test still runs, but no test names AC-5 any more, which hides the item's only evidence.
findings.fix: Restore the title 'AC-5: each view links to the other'.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but a commit after the go rewrote AC-5 in the spec. The PR also says 'test/starred.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-7', which is no longer true by name for AC-5.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edits, or disclose them truthfully and record the owner's decision in the spec.

findings.what: The check now accepts any query string and rejects only whitespace and '#'. This is disclosed in the PR. The new tests cover a fragment, a space, and an accepted query.

lenses.note: The spec has a recorded go. The change implements it, apart from the late AC-5 edit.
The late commit edited AC-5 without a recorded owner decision. All four state-table rows have tests.
I could not run the suite because vitest is not installed (npm test: vitest not found). I judged the tests by reading them. AC-5 is no longer named by any test.
The view is validated with Object.hasOwn. The SQL is built only from fixed view definitions, with no user input.
The show parameter is allow-listed. Titles are escaped. I found no injection path.
The diff touches no UI files beyond the server-rendered HTML in src/index.js, and no browser evidence exists.
The diff touches no frontend files and the PR has no preview.
The claim 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false, because AC-5 was edited after the go.
